brief: UBS's Ali Baig attributes this week's sharp Treasury rally (10s ~35bps off the 5.31% high) to CTA/algo futures flows and Fast Money short covering into the October FOMC, not a change in inflation views: firmer CPI/PPI and a still-tightening-biased Fed (even with an expected October pass) leave Real Money questioning the rally's sustainability, and breakevens haven't followed because the rates complex's reaction function has shifted toward weighting AI capex/financing and growth risk over inflation surprises. He holds a long-standing view that a bad-tail tech-bubble pop forces a Fed cut in late 2027/2028, but says it's too early to call that materializing now. Near term, duration needs another 5-10bp rally before systematic CTA/risk-parity demand strengthens materially, which could reinforce convexity receiving and further short-covering. He fades the long end (likes 10x5/15x5 steepeners, short 30y MMS) given its high beta to oil-driven risk, arguing delivered energy costs and disruption premia haven't normalized even as Hormuz flows recover. He also argues hyperscalers shifting from debt to equity financing for projected $1.6-1.8tn of 2027-28 AI capex means less rate-lock supply than feared, a bullish-duration, bearish-AI-capex-story development.
